== Who I am ==

My name is Edward Stewart Hore, and I go by Stewart. I have been a member of
the Ubuntu Kernel Team since January 2025.

I graduated with a PhD in Computer Science and Mathematics in 2005. Before
joining Canonical I worked as a software engineer in computer games, the Earth
sciences, telco network engineering, and regulated software for medical and
automotive devices. The regulated work in particular taught me the habits this
role needs: careful review, reproducible builds, and a lot of respect for the
cost of shipping a defect to someone who cannot easily roll back.

=== My Ubuntu story ===

I have run Ubuntu since 6.06 "Dapper Drake". It has been my development
operating system for most of my career, and it is what I reach for whenever I
have a server or a cloud instance to look after, both privately and
professionally.

=== My involvement ===

I have contributed to SRU cycles since joining the kernel team, across
linux-aws(-6.8), linux-gcp(-5.15/-6.8), linux-ibm-6.8, linux-oracle-6.8,
linux-xilinx, linux-xilinx-zynqmp and linux-kvm, together with their meta,
signed and restricted-modules companions, on focal, jammy and noble.

Beyond the regular cranks:

* I was the maintainer for the Xilinx kernels, linux-xilinx and
   linux-xilinx-zynqmp, from June 2025 to June 2026.
* I am currently working on the NXP 7.0 kernel. It is still in development
   and is not yet part of the SRU and SWM workflows, so it does not appear in
   the upload log below.
* I work on hardware enablement and backporting.
* I have found and fixed bugs in the kernel team's regression testing
   infrastructure, so that the results the rest of the team relies on are
   trustworthy.
* I have worked on the kernel snapcraft plugin, and fixed a number of bugs in
   the existing kernel snapcraft builds for the Xilinx kernels.

Upload rights would let me land these cycles without taking up a sponsor's
time on every one, and would let me sponsor for others in turn, which is the
part I am most looking forward to.

=== Sponsoring ===

Since joining Canonical in January 2025 I have had 94 package uploads
sponsored, between 2025-02-20 and 2026-04-27, spanning linux-aws(-6.8),
linux-gcp(-5.15/-6.8), linux-ibm-6.8, linux-oracle-6.8, linux-xilinx,
linux-xilinx-zynqmp and linux-kvm, and their meta, signed and
restricted-modules companions, across focal, jammy and noble.
